column1: # lucian-uxui catalog · api v1 · lang=en · count=400 · version=34c4b3e61d · https://lucianlabs.dev/uxui-prompt/

column8: summary
A glass capsule with light caught inside. Press it and it shrinks like a water drop to show loading, then expands again with a check mark.

The button and its label are pulled toward the cursor at different depths. Hover and the circle on the right floods the whole button; press it and the arrow shoots out and comes back from the other side.
To prevent accidental deletes, a red fill rises only while you keep the button pressed. When it is full the file crumples away, and Undo brings it right back.
Press it and the arrow drops while the button itself turns into a progress bar. When the download finishes it folds into a circle, draws a check and opens up again as saved.

Press send and the paper plane inside the button lifts off, loops once and flies off the screen, leaving a dotted trail that fades away. Meanwhile a progress ring circles the button and turns into a check, and the message rises into the chat as a bubble. A moment later a new plane glides back into the button.
Ink spreads from the exact spot you press and the button switches to subscribed. The bell shakes and the subscriber count rolls up by one. Press again to reverse it.

column5: button play pause morph audio progress
column8: The play triangle splits into two pieces and becomes the pause bars. While playing, the outer ring and the waveform fill up together, and you can press the waveform to jump to any point.

column4: Copy button that turns into a check
column8: Copies the install command in one go. Press it and the stacked-squares icon is redrawn as a check, a gleam passes over the command, and a “Copied” bubble pops up.
Hover and the letters roll up one by one while the arrow slips out and comes back in. Press it and color rises from the bottom into a selected state.

The main action and its options sit in one control. Press the arrow and the menu unfolds from the button’s corner; the option you pick rolls into the main label. Run it and a progress bar flows inside the button before it turns into done.
The plus button spins into a close icon and four create actions pop out one after another in a fan. Pick one and the menu folds away while the result floats up for a moment.
Press it and color pours down into the ribbon from the top, the icon drops and bounces back up, and small confetti scatters. The save count and the label roll over together.

While it travels, the knob stretches like rubber and then snaps back into place. The symbol inside the knob is redrawn from ✕ to ✓ and the caption below changes with the state. You can also drag the knob.

Check an item and the circle fills with color, a check is drawn, then a strike-through sweeps across the task from the left. The progress ring at the top fills along, and turns into a done mark when everything is finished.
The frame slides over to the plan you choose, and the dot inside the circle pops in. The price only comes to full strength on the selected plan.
Stars fill in ahead of time as far as the cursor goes, and when you press they pop up one after another from the left with a sparkle. A matching word and color change with the score.
The value bubble above leans away from the direction you drag, as far as your speed, then springs upright when you stop. The fill bar and the tick labels respond to the value too.
Press plus or minus and the number rolls one notch like an odometer. The total counts along smoothly, and at the minimum or maximum the stepper shakes its head.
Pick a chip and a check slides out from the left as it fills with color. You can pick up to five; try a sixth and the chip shakes its head while the counter flashes a warning.
Pick a color and it fills the tumbler from the bottom while the glow behind takes on the same color. The selection ring glides to your pick and the color name rolls over.
The sun knob rolls across and turns into a cratered moon. The sky deepens to night, the clouds sink away and the stars start to twinkle.
The heart crouches, fills with red and leaps, while a ring and little dots burst out around it. The like count rolls up by one; press again and it quietly goes back.
Turn a switch on and its detailed options unfold below it. “Turn all off” switches everything off one by one from the top, and the icons of switched-off items fade to gray.
Choose a price range with two handles: bars outside the range sink while only the bars inside rise in color. The result count rolls over and the price at the top updates with it.
Focus a field and its label shrinks and rises into a notch in the border, which parts around it. A valid email draws a check; an invalid one shakes the field and drops down a hint.

Each digit pops up from below as you fill a box, and the cursor moves on to the next. With all six filled the boxes ripple while checking — green if it matches, or a shake and an empty row if it does not.

Press the magnifier in the top bar and the menu steps aside while the search field stretches across the bar. Recent searches and suggestions unfold below; as you type, results filter and the matching letters are highlighted.
The box grows smoothly as you write, and the ring in the bottom-right fills as you use up characters. Near the limit the ring turns orange, past it red, and it shows how many are left as a number.

Press Enter and the text pops out as a colored tag; press a suggestion chip and it jumps into the field. In an empty field, Backspace once highlights the last tag for removal and a second press removes it.

Press a start date and the range band follows your cursor; press an end date and the band locks in. Change months and the date grid slides sideways, while the two fields at the top and the summary below update together.

Press the field and the list grows open right below it, with a check on the current value. Move with the arrow keys and the highlight bar glides along; type a letter to jump straight to items that start with it.
Drag files in and the dashed border starts marching as the area grows; each dropped file fills its own progress bar in the list below. Finished files draw a check, and failed ones can be retried.

Press the title and it becomes a field in the very same type, with an underline drawn from the left. Save with Enter and a green gleam sweeps across while the edit time updates; Esc puts the original title back.

As you type, the rest of the name appears faintly and Tab accepts it. The list below filters with the matching letters highlighted, and the highlight bar glides along with the arrow keys. Choosing one locks it in with a plane icon.

Only the digits that change pop up from below as you type, and thousands separators slip in naturally. Quick-amount chips add to it, and going over your balance turns the amount red with a shake and blocks Send.
With every keystroke the four-part bar fills and shifts from red to green, and each rule you satisfy pops its circle into a check. Press the eye icon and its lid opens to reveal the password.

Press the account chip at the bottom and the menu grows upward out of it while the items float in one by one. A highlight bar follows the cursor, and picking another workspace updates the chip’s name and color as the menu folds away.

Right-click a file or press ⋯ and the menu blooms from the cursor. Near an edge it opens the other way, and the Share item slides its submenu in from the side. Deleting folds the card away with an undo.
Press a tab and the black pill stretches and glides over to it, while the list below slides in row by row from the direction you moved.
The icon-only rail widens as the menu names follow out line by line, pushing the screen beside it over. Choose an item and the highlight slides up or down while the screen title on the right changes.
A round button rises above the selected tab while the top edge of the bar dips into a matching notch and slides along with it. The icon lifts up into the circle and the label appears below.

Press Next and the progress line fills up to the next circle while finished steps turn into checks. The content slides in the direction you are moving, and on the last step the button becomes “Get started”.

Change pages and the highlight pill stretches out from the leading edge, then catches up from behind as it arrives. The big page number rolls up or down, and the artwork tiles above come in one after another from the direction you moved.
Press a question and its panel lifts as the answer unfolds smoothly, while one stroke of the plus lies down to become a minus. Only one opens at a time; the rest fold away calmly.

column5: hamburger menu fullscreen clip-path stagger focus-trap
column8: While the hamburger’s three lines fold into an ×, the menu screen spreads out as a circle from the button and covers the screen. The page behind steps back slightly, and the big menu words rise line by line.

The search pill unfolds downward into a palette; as you type, results filter with the matching letters highlighted. The highlight bar glides to the chosen item, and running it folds the palette back into a pill.
Switch the period and the knob stretches as it moves, the big number counts from the old value to the new one, and the chart line bends into its new shape.
Swipe the articles sideways and the underline stretches along with your finger to the next tab. The chosen tab scrolls to the center, and both ends of the tab row fade to hint there is more.
Move the cursor and the sun and hills in the illustration shift at different depths. Hover or focus and the title rises to reveal a summary and a Read button; on touch, a single tap opens it.

The card tilts toward the cursor while the surface glare and the border light gather at the same spot. Press “Mark as read” and the unread dot drops away, the headline quiets down and the button turns into a check.
Pick a color and the bottle refills with it from the top. Press Add and a small bottle arcs up into the cart in the top right, which wobbles as its count goes up.

Drag the card sideways and it turns in 3D with your hand, then snaps to the nearest face when you let go. A simple press flips it too, and the holographic sheen on the front flows with the tilt. Locking it sinks the card into grayscale.

Drag the top card and it tilts with your hand while a SAVE or PASS stamp darkens depending on the direction. Throw it far enough and it spins away as the next card rises. Undo brings back the card you just swiped.

Press Follow and the button turns into “Following” with a check, while only the changed digits of the follower count roll. The lower panel slides from recent posts to “similar people” suggestions, and hovering the Following button turns it into an unfollow prompt.

Press play and the record slides out of its sleeve and spins while the tonearm lowers onto it. Skip to the next track and the sleeve swaps sideways as the record’s label color changes. Drag the progress bar to seek.

Switch between monthly and yearly and only the changed digits of each price roll down, while the “2 months free” badge wiggles. Pick a plan and the highlight frame slides over, with the feature list and the start button text changing along.

Reviews advance every few seconds; in the row of faces below, the current speaker grows and a ring around them fills with the time left. The quote fades in word by word, and you can drag sideways or press a face to jump.

Scroll the article and the top line and the ring on the right fill up while the time left goes down. The highlight pill follows to the contents chip of the section you are reading, and when you reach the end the ring turns into a check.

Choose “Going” and your face pushes into the front of the attendee row while the head count rolls up, a little confetti bursts and an Add to Calendar button unfolds. Switch to “Can’t go” and your face drops out as the row closes up again.
Split the same city by day and by night with a handle. The handle grows while you drag, pressing anywhere makes it spring to that spot, and the labels fade as the divider approaches them.

Press a photo and it grows from its thumbnail to fill the frame; close it and it shrinks back into place. In the viewer, double-click to zoom and drag around, swipe sideways to move between photos, or drag down to close.

Press Sign in and the button shrinks into a spinning circle. A wrong password shakes the card like a head-shake and tells you how many tries are left; the right one turns the button into a check and the card moves on to a welcome screen. The eye on the show-password button blinks open.

Questions rise one at a time, and each answer folds up into a summary chip at the top. A wrong format shakes the field and explains why, and the bar at the top fills one segment per step. Press a summary chip to go back to that question.
Press the button and the letter slides down into the envelope, the flap closes and the envelope flies off. A “Check your inbox” screen opens next, with Resend locked until its ring fills.

When a sign-in request comes from a new device, the time left shrinks around a ring and the location dot pulses like a heartbeat. Pick the number shown on the other screen to approve with a check; a wrong pick shakes, and denying turns it into a red shield.

Pick a provider and the other buttons fold away, leaving only yours with a connecting spinner. Once connected the button becomes an account row, and “Use another method” unfolds the hidden buttons again one by one.

An account locked after too many failed sign-ins. The ring around the padlock shrinks with the time left as the digits tick over; when time is up the shackle springs open and “Sign in again” lights up. You can also send a reset email instead of waiting.

The border bar fills as you scroll the terms, and reaching the end unlocks the required consents as their checks pop out. “Agree to all” checks the items below one after another, and the start button turns on once every required item is chosen.

Drag the photo inside the round frame and zoom with the slider or the wheel; rule-of-thirds guides appear while you drag and everything outside the frame dims. Rotation springs around, and saving flies the cropped circle up into the profile spot.

A new toast rises from the bottom to the front while earlier ones tuck behind it, shrinking. Hover and the stack fans out into a list and stops auto-dismissing; swipe a toast sideways to remove just that one. The “Saving” toast spins and then turns into done.

Swipe an email left to reveal the red layer behind it as the trash icon grows; swipe far enough and the row folds away. A snackbar rises with a ring counting down, and Undo unfolds the deleted rows back into place.

Alert rows stack up, each with its own color and icon. Dismiss one and it slides aside as its height folds, letting the rows below move up. The error alert expands a log with Details, and once all are dismissed a button to bring them back appears.

Announcements roll upward in the strip at the top of the page while short bars on the right fill with the time left. Hovering pauses it; closing folds the strip away and the page below moves up. After closing, a small bell button brings it back.

When a new notification arrives the bell shakes, the badge count pops, and a new row pushes in at the top of the open list. Clicking an item clears its unread dot, and “Mark all read” clears the dots one by one. The bell folds the list into itself and back out.

As files upload, the ring in the panel header fills with overall progress and counts down the time left. Each file’s bar fills and turns into a check when done, while a failed file stops in red and shows a retry button. Clicking the header folds and unfolds the list.

Rest on a tool button and a tooltip rises after a short delay; move to the next button and it glides along with no wait. It opens downward from the top bar and upward from the bottom bar, and at the edges only the box shifts inward while the arrow keeps pointing at the button.

The popover grows out of the “Add reaction” button with its arrow pointing back at it. Pick an emoji and a reaction chip pops up with its count rising while the popover shrinks back into the button. Clicking outside or pressing Esc also closes it.

Swipe a message right and the reply arrow fills; let go and a quote line rises above the composer. Typing turns the mic into a send button, and the sent bubble rises out of the composer before the other person’s typing dots and reply arrive.

column4: Skeleton that blooms into a post
column8: A single streak of light sweeps the whole grey skeleton in one beat. When loading finishes, the profile, photo and text turn into their real selves from the top down, and the photo starts blurred before coming into focus.

Planets circle three tilted orbits at different speeds while the core glows like it is breathing. The step text and counter change, and at the end the orbits are drawn into the core, which turns into a check as a ripple spreads.

Press pay and the button shrinks into a circle as a ring draws itself once around, lighting up the steps below in turn. When the ring fills it turns green and draws a check, and the receipt slides up from below.

A dark veil over the app icon sweeps away clockwise to show install progress while the percentage and speed below climb with it. Tapping the icon switches to a pause mark and stops it, and when it finishes the icon bounces and an “Open” button appears.

While queued with no known end, two bar segments stretch and slide; once the build starts, the same bar smoothly turns into a progress bar that fills. Log lines rise one by one as spinners turn into checks, and the status pill changes its color and text along with it.

While the mic button is held, five dots stretch up and down with the loudness of your voice. Let go and they turn into a rolling wave that shows it’s thinking, and then the transcribed sentence appears letter by letter.

Pull the list down and it follows like a rubber band, getting heavier as it goes, while the arrow circle at the top draws and spins as far as you pull. Past the threshold the circle fills and the text turns into “Release to refresh”; let go and it spins while new posts slide in from the top.

Send a question and three dots bounce to show it’s thinking, then the answer flows out word by word, each one floating up slightly. A cursor blinks at the end, and the stop button turns into “Regenerate” once it finishes.

Each time the delivery stage changes, a small truck drives along the line to the next dot and the road behind it fills with color. New stages push in at the top of the log below, and on arrival the truck stops and turns into a check flag.

With no projects, an empty folder floats slowly; hover a template and the folder opens a little as a sheet of paper peeks out. Pick a template and the paper flies in, the folder gulps it down and the first item becomes a list, and when everything is deleted the folder settles back down.

The middle 0 of 404 is a compass whose needle springs after the cursor, and the digits on either side lean toward it. Pick a similar address and the typo in the address bar is erased and retyped, the digits roll to 200 and the needle spins once before settling on north.

column4: Error widget that plugs back in
column8: A widget that failed to load waits with its plug pulled, while the ring around the button shrinks to show the time until it retries on its own. On retry the plug moves in and wobbles; if it fails it bounces back with sparks, and if it works it plugs in, the light turns green and the chart grows.

When the connection drops, a banner comes down with Wi‑Fi arcs blinking in turn as it searches for a signal, and messages sent in the meantime wait in dashed bubbles with a clock mark. Reconnect and the slash wipes away, the banner turns green, and the queued messages fill in and send one by one.

With no results, a magnifier sweeps the empty shelves, and the screen works out how many items each filter would give if removed and offers that as a button. Press the button or a chip’s × and the chip folds away while only the newly matching products float up one by one.

column4: Celebration when every task is done
column8: Each time you check a task, small dots burst from the box, the text is struck through and the bar at the top fills. Check the last one and confetti bursts upward and drifts down as a celebration sheet rises and the badge and streak number roll up.

Drag the time bar below and the sky shifts through dawn, day, sunset and night while the sun and moon rise and set along a dotted arc. Cloud cover, rain, stars and the temperature all change to match that hour.

Switch between week, month and year and the bars don’t regrow; their count, width and height carry over into the new shape while the axis numbers and average line move along. Sweep across the bars and only the one under you darkens while the big number and tooltip switch to its value and change from the previous one.

column4: Stock line that splits as you scrub
column8: Scrub along the line and it splits into color to the left of the cursor and grey to the right, while the price, change and date at the top switch to that point. Dropping below the starting point turns the line and area red; let go and the cursor returns to now, and changing the period morphs the line into its new shape.

Hover a donut slice and it slides outward and thickens while the center switches to that category’s amount and share. Click a slice or legend item and it drops out as the remaining slices share its angle and close the circle again, with the total rolling along.

Each digit of the big number rolls on its own, so when the value changes only the digits that differ spin up or down. The trend line below shifts one step left with every new value, and switching metrics rolls the number up from zero while the line morphs into its new shape.

Three rings fill one after another toward the center, and a ring past its goal carries a shadowed tip as it laps a second time. Pick a weekday below and the rings shrink or grow into that day’s values; the moment a ring closes it flashes once while the numbers on the right roll along.

The top half of each digit card folds forward from the center hinge and the bottom half follows, unfolding into the next number. Only the digits that change flip; in the last 10 seconds the digits turn orange, and when it ends the cards shake once and a restart button appears.
A split view with a document beside its cover preview. Drag the divider to resize both panes, or set the same widths from the keyboard.
A tree for opening and closing folders to pick a file. An opened folder shows its contents indented below, and the chosen file stays highlighted.
A one-line path through nested folders. Press a parent to climb back up, then pick a subfolder below to go down again.
A view onto part of a large artboard, with a minimap of the whole. Move the purple frame in the minimap and the view follows to that spot.
A studio floor plan where you choose a room. The room you press is highlighted along with its name and area.
A seat map from a ticketing screen. Press an open seat to select it and press again to release it; your seats and the total appear below.
Compare a direct and a transfer route on the line map. Pick a route and its stretch of line darkens while its travel time is highlighted.
A meeting planner that lines up the time in Seoul, London and New York. Move the UTC time and all three clocks and their work status change together.
A grid for painting the hours you’re free this week. Press a cell or drag across several to fill them at once, and the total updates right away.
A timeline showing two overlapping meetings. One button moves the later meeting into free time, and pressing it again puts it back.
A Gantt editor for changing a task’s start day and length on a weekly chart. Drag the bar to move its start or the end handle to change its length, and the summary follows.
An 8-step drum sequencer with kick, snare and hat rows. Press pads to switch them on or off, and press play to watch the current beat sweep from left to right.
A workbench for drawing a small icon on an 8×8 grid. Press an empty cell to fill it or a filled one to erase it; drag to change every cell you pass over.
A pen tool for shaping a curve with two control points. Drag a handle at the end of a dotted line and the curve bends with it; the points also move from the keyboard.
An editor for placing the middle color of a three-color gradient. Move the middle stop and the point where the colors blend shifts, with its position shown below.

An editor for building an animation’s timing curve. Drag the pink and teal control points and the curve and its cubic-bezier value update instantly, while a dot traveling along the curve and the ball below move exactly as the curve says. A faint ball runs at constant speed (linear) for comparison, and presets glide the control points to their values.
A measuring tool for the gap between two objects. Move the slider and the objects spread apart or close in, with the dimension line and px value following along.
A specimen for comparing font weights at a glance. Move the weight slider and both sample lines switch to that weight, with its value shown.
A card sample that pairs a tight contact shadow with a wide ambient one. Raise the elevation and the card lifts while both shadows change in proportion.
A sample that rounds all four corners together. Drag the corner handle and every corner follows while the radius value updates.
A grid where four blocks rearrange to fit the number of columns. Change the columns with the slider and the blocks move into their new places.
A panel for reordering three overlapping layers. Press a layer to bring it to the front; the new order is announced to screen readers too.
A sample that compares blend modes where two colored circles overlap. Each press of the button cycles through six modes, including multiply, screen and overlay.
A checker that calculates text and background contrast as you type. Change a color and the preview and ratio update, along with whether normal text passes AA.
A canvas where a shape snaps to the center guides as you move it. Near the middle a guide line appears and locks it in place; Enter centers it right away.
A note that flips between its rendered preview and the Markdown source on one sheet. Press Edit to open the source, then press it again to see headings, lists and bold text rendered.
A review panel for accepting one code change or keeping the original. Accept and the removed line disappears; reject and the added line goes, leaving only the final code.
A find-and-replace panel that highlights matches in the text and changes them all at once. Type a word and its matches light up; Replace all fixes every one.
An editor that folds and unfolds code one function at a time. Folding hides the body lines, and the line numbers skip ahead to match.
A mapping screen that links each CSV column to a field in your service. Pick a target field from the list to change a link, and a warning appears as soon as two columns share a field.
A repeating group that takes the same details for each person in your party. Add creates a new numbered row, and each row can be removed on its own.
A rule editor that combines purchase count and region with AND/OR to pick an audience. Change a value or the connector and the matching count updates instantly.
A converter that switches a length between two units as you type. Edit either side and the other recalculates; change a unit and the result follows.
A receipt that splits a total by each person’s share. Change a share and everyone’s amount recalculates in proportion while the total still adds up.
A recipe card whose ingredients scale with the number of servings. Change the servings with + and − and every ingredient recalculates in the same proportion.
An editor that sets the recipient’s address right on the envelope. Edit the name or address and the lettering on the envelope updates in place.
A practice card that groups the number into blocks of four. Type digits and the number on the card regroups instantly, with the brand detected from the first digits.
An editor for hiding sensitive parts of a document, like names and email addresses. Press a marked span to black it out, and press again to bring the text back.
An annotation editor that pins a margin note to each sentence. Press the mark after a sentence to open its note; whatever you type stays attached to that sentence.
A formatting bar that bolds or italicizes the selected text and changes paragraph alignment. With nothing selected it applies to the whole paragraph, and each button shows the current state.
A field for setting a shortcut by pressing it. Press the keycaps to start recording, and the combination you press with a modifier becomes the new shortcut.
An alignment tool for pairing English source phrases with their Korean translations. Pick a phrase on the left, then press its translation on the right to tie them with the same number.
A tiny sheet where editing a number recalculates the totals right away. Each column sum and the grand total update together.
A column editor for hiding table columns or moving them forward. Press a header to open a small menu, and the table redraws as soon as you choose.
An editor for correcting a transcript one word at a time. Every word carries its timestamp, so you can fix just the one that’s wrong.
An editor that lays nested JSON out as a tree so you can change values in place. Strings, numbers and booleans each get the right kind of input, so their types stay intact.
A test field that highlights what your regular expression matches in the text below as you type. It counts the matches and flags syntax errors.
An editor that typesets a reference from author, year, title and publisher fields. Edit a field and the citation resets instantly; the button switches between APA and MLA.
A merge view for lines where your version and your team’s collide. Choose one side for each line and the final document comes together in place.
A tidy-up tool that strips stray spaces and duplicates from a list and sorts it. Each button applies one cleanup instantly, and Ctrl/⌘+Z undoes it.
A heatmap of 84 days of contributions laid out week by week. Move the date slider and that day’s cell is marked, with its date and count shown below.
A treemap that splits storage into areas sized by each folder. Press a folder tile to go inside, and use the arrow to climb back up.
A Sankey diagram tracing how visits from each channel flow through interest to purchase. Press a channel to keep only its flow; press it again to see them all.
A radar chart that overlays two people’s skills on five axes. Pick a person in the legend to bring their shape forward and show their strongest skill.
A scatter plot with one dot per experiment, by cost and accuracy. Turn on the cost filter to fade dots above the limit, or press a dot to see that experiment’s numbers.
A box-and-whisker summary of response times. Press the outlying dot to see that request’s details, and press again to return to the summary.
A stacked area chart showing a week of usage by service. Pick a service in the legend to keep only its layer, with its usage and share shown.
A waterfall chart that walks from a starting value through gains and costs to the total. Switch off “With costs” and the cost bars fade while the total recalculates.
A candlestick chart of five trading days, with open, high, low and close. Pick a candle to see that day’s four prices and its change below.
A funnel showing how many people drop off at each step from visit to purchase. Press a step to see its biggest drop-off reason, and press again to return to the overall rate.
A cohort table that shades each cell by how many customers from a signup week were still around weeks later. Press a cell to highlight that retention, and press again to clear it.
A matrix that colors the correlation between four variables. Press a cell to show that pair and its coefficient below, and press again to clear it.
A bullet chart that layers the actual bar and the target mark on one line. Move the target slider and the mark shifts while the gap and attainment recalculate.
A histogram that groups response-time samples into bins. Change the number of bins and the bars regroup, with the busiest range called out.
A forecast chart that spreads a band of possible values beyond the observed line. Switch between the 80% and 95% intervals and the band’s width and range change together.
A log viewer that lists server logs in time order. Turn on “Errors only” to keep just the error lines, and press again to see everything.
A trace view that breaks one request into nested spans. Press a bar to highlight that call and show how long it took; press again to clear it.
A waterfall that splits each request on a page into waiting, TLS and transfer time. Press a request to highlight its transfer time, and press again to see the full load time.
A schema map that draws the key relationships between tables. Press a table to highlight only its links, with the keys that connect them shown below.

column4: Timeline that zooms into an incident
column8: A timeline that lays the window from detection to recovery, and its events, over an error-rate chart. In the full view, clustered events show as a single bundle; zoom in and the axis stretches smoothly so only the incident fills the width and the events spread apart one by one. Press an event to see its time and details below, while the minimap shows the range you are looking at.
A resource allocator for three teams sharing 12 cores. Change a team’s number and the bar above redivides, with each maximum adjusted so the total never goes over.
A depth chart that steps out how much is waiting to buy and sell at each price. Move the price and the cursor follows, with the cumulative size up to that price shown.
A compass that shows the gap between the sensor’s reading and a reference heading. Move the reference and both needles turn; press calibrate to line the reading up with it.
A wind rose that fans out how often the wind came from each direction. Pick a direction to see its count and share, or switch on “Strong only” to redraw just the high winds.
A chart that puts product metrics with different units on their own rails. Press “Normalize” and weight, battery and price all become 0–100 scores, so better and worse read at a glance.
A filmstrip of a document’s earlier versions. Pick one and the large preview switches to it; press restore to make it the current version.

Each edit to the shape stacks up as a node in the history graph below. Undo a few steps and make a new edit, and the history that used to follow isn’t thrown away — it stays as a branch on the row below, and pressing any node smoothly returns the shape to that state. The current position wears a ring, and steps you can still redo are shown faded.
A workbench for acting on several files at once. Select files and a bulk-action bar appears below; after archiving you can undo right away.
A clipboard that keeps copied snippets on a shelf so you can pick and paste them. Snippets join the sentence below in the order you press them, and clear starts over.
An approval line that collects three signatures in order: drafted, reviewed, approved. Each press stamps the next box, and after final approval you can start over.
A dispatcher that assigns incoming tasks by each person’s remaining capacity. Press a person to hand them the top task; their fill rises and the next task comes up.
A queue display for taking tickets and calling the next number at a counter. Taking a ticket grows the waiting list; calling flips the big number and shortens it.
A ranked-choice ballot where you reorder the options before voting. Move an option up one place with its arrow, and voting scores each one by its rank.
A permissions table for switching view, edit and share on or off for each role. Press a cell to flip that permission; the owner’s essential rights are locked on.
A vault that walks through replacing an API key step by step. Rotating puts the new key into use while the old one gets a grace period, and the next step revokes it.

A radar screen for finding and connecting nearby devices. Press Find and a beam sweeps around once every 1.6 seconds while waves ripple out from the center, and each device flashes into view the moment the beam passes its direction. Press a device and a signal flows along a line from the center until it connects; press again and the line retracts as it disconnects.
A screen for scanning a ticket at the door. Press the ticket and it goes through a check to admitted; press again and a fresh ticket is issued.
A canary release screen that opens a new feature to a slice of users first. Each step raises the share and fills that much of the dot grid, and roll back undoes it at once.
A promotion gate that moves a release through dev, staging and production. Each press runs a check, then advances to the next environment; at the end you can start over.
An outbox holding a scheduled email. Press the scheduled time to change it, or press the arrow to send it right away.

A player that replays recorded user input on a tiny sign-up screen. Press play and the cursor glides exactly as recorded, pressing fields and typing one character at a time, with a ripple wherever it clicks. The tape below color-codes moves, clicks and typing; drag the playhead to scrub back and forth, or press → to skip to the next event.
A mixer for balancing voice, music and ambience. Move a fader to set its level or press a channel name to mute it; no actual sound plays.
A breathing guide that paces a 4-second inhale, 2-second hold and 4-second exhale with the size of a circle. Press the circle to start, with the seconds left shown; press again to stop.
A loop editor for marking the stretch of a waveform to repeat. Move the handles and the length recalculates; press play and only that region repeats (silently).
A player that splits a video into chapters on a rail. Press a chapter and the preview scene and playback time jump there together.
A co-editing screen for passing edit control between people. Press someone’s cursor to hand them control, and the shape follows their edits.

A tour that highlights the key controls of a real app screen one by one. Press Take the tour and the screen dims while only the first target shows through a rounded hole; each Next glides the hole to the size and position of the next target. The explanation bubble follows with a tail pointing at the target, and a glowing ring pulses around the hole.
A diagnostic screen that checks the path from a device to the origin server hop by hop. The probe stops at the failing hop, and reroute restores the connection another way.
A verifier that hashes a document and checks it against the original. Change a single character and the checksum changes at once, flagging the mismatch (FNV-1a demo).
A receipt folded down to just its total. Press details and the paper unfolds to show the items and VAT; press again to fold it back.

A workflow that sorts new inquiries automatically. Press Run and the inquiry form step at the top completes, then a glowing dot travels down the connector and the AI classification step starts spinning. When classification finishes its result is written in, and dots flow down both branches at once so the alert and contact list steps complete in turn, with each step's time and the total run time shown.

Six months of results for four regions, shown as a block city seen from an angle. Blocks rise row by row from the front when it first appears, and switching between orders and visits with the chips above re-levels the heights in a wave. Hover a block and only its row and column keep their color while the rest turns gray, and its value floats up.

A front view of premium headphones: a slim stainless steel frame runs straight down into both arms, a knit-mesh canopy hangs from its ends like a hammock, and the arms hold aluminum ear cups with mesh cushions on the inside. Hover a softly pulsing pin and a dotted line draws from it down to a note card that slides up, while that part brightens and the rest dims. On the crown pin the dial's ridges turn, and on the mic pin sound waves ripple out and get cancelled. Press a color dot below and the cups, canopy and cushions blend to the new finish as the color name rolls over.

Thirty-six project bubbles, each sized by budget, sit in one cluster; pick By team or By status in the tabs above and they jostle apart and gather into new groups. Each group carries its name and budget total along with it, and hovering a bubble shows that project's team, status and budget in a tooltip.

Letters near the cursor rise and settle, and their neighbours follow less the farther away they are. Each letter wobbles on its own spring before coming to rest, and the higher it rises the more its color blooms and its floor shadow shrinks. Press the button to send one big wave from left to right.

A network with me in the middle, linked to work, college and neighborhood friends by spring-like lines. Drag any dot and its connections trail after it, bouncing, then push and pull back into place when you let go. Press a dot to keep only that person's direct links and see their group and number of connections below.

In a landing page's testimonials section, review cards flow endlessly in two vertical columns, the left one moving up and the right one moving down at different speeds. The top and bottom edges fade softly, and the key sentence in each card is highlighted. Rest the pointer on a column and only that column stops while the card you point at lifts slightly.

App icons lined up in a dock at the bottom of the screen grow and rise smoothly the closer the cursor gets, with neighbors stepping aside to make room. The icon right under the cursor shows a name tag; press it and it bounces as it launches, lighting a running dot beneath. When the cursor leaves, everything settles back to normal size.

Pick a country from the button on the left of a phone field and the flag and dialing code spin to the new country, while the digits you've typed regroup into that country's format. Hyphens or parentheses drop into place as you type, and when the length is right a check appears and the Send code button turns on; too few or too many digits bring down a hint. The country list can be searched by name.

column4: Webinar sign-up card with a growing crowd
column8: In a live webinar sign-up card, every few seconds a new attendee pops in at the front of the overlapping avatar stack, nudging the others aside, as the sign-up count rolls up digit by digit. Rest the pointer on the stack and the photos fan out, showing the name of the person you point at. Press Save my seat and the button spins briefly before confirming, while your own avatar slips in at the front with a ring burst.

A sign-up section at the end of a page: a faint grid and a beam of light turn behind the button, the “free for 14 days” line carries a flowing band of the button's colors, and colored light slowly circles the main button. Hover and the light speeds up as the button lifts slightly and the arrow pushes forward. Press it and three dots bounce inside before it turns into a check with ‘Check your inbox’, a faint green ring ripples out once from the button, the team count at the top rolls up by one, and the reassurance line changes.

At the top, a roomy transparent header sits over the page; scroll down and it slides up out of the way to give you room to read. Scroll up even a little and it comes back down as a slim header with a blurred background and shadow, while a thin bar beneath it fills as you read. Back at the very top it turns transparent again.

A landing page's feature tabs move to the next tab every few seconds, and the bar under the current tab fills with the time left. When the tab changes, the product screen below swaps and plays its scene: calendar blocks drop into place, document lines write themselves, or chart bars grow. Press a tab to jump straight to it, and rest the pointer on the screen to pause the bar.

Features are introduced in a bento grid of interlocking tiles of different sizes. Hover a tile and it lifts slightly with a brighter border while its own little scene plays: the collaboration tile gathers avatars and types text, the search tile enters a query, the stats tile grows bars, the security tile pulses its shield, and the integrations tile scrolls a row of icons.

column4: Support chat from a launcher bubble
column8: Press the chat bubble in the bottom right of a website and the support window grows out from where the button was, showing the team's faces and “We usually reply in 3 minutes.” Press a quick question chip and your bubble rises, three dots bounce, and an answer arrives with a help article card. Choose Talk to a person and a line announces an agent has joined before their first hello arrives.

The moment a landing page's first screen appears, the top menu settles in, then the badge, headline words, description, two buttons and product screen rise from below one after another at short intervals. Each headline word slides up from beneath a hidden line, and the product screen arrives tilted back and blurred before straightening into focus. Use Replay in the top right to watch the entrance again.

A table comparing the features of three plans row by row. The plan name row stays pinned to the top as you scroll, and resting the pointer on a cell lights up that plan's whole column and darkens its select button at the top. Turn on Differences only and rows that are the same across all three plans fold away, and groups that empty out fold along with their titles.

column4: Mini player that docks on scroll
column8: Press play on the big player at the top of a podcast page and the sound bars dance as the progress bar runs. Scroll down until the big player leaves the screen and it shrinks into a mini bar docked at the bottom, keeping its playback and progress. Press the mini bar and the page glides back up to the big player.

Press the sun icon in the site header and a dark screen spreads out in a circle from that button until it covers the whole page, as the icon spins from sun to moon. Press it again and the light screen spreads back from the same spot. Text, cards and charts all change color with the theme.

In a blog post, drag to select a sentence or press one, and a small tooltip pops up above it with highlight, copy and share buttons. Press highlight and color paints in beneath the sentence from left to right and stays; press copy and the button turns into a check as a ‘Quote copied’ notice slides up from below.

column4: Sticky buy bar with option sheet
column8: Scroll down a product page until the buy button in the content leaves the screen, and a bar with the price and a buy button rises from below and sticks; scroll back up to the original button and the bar slips away. Press Buy on the bar and it stretches upward into a size sheet, and the add button only turns on once you choose a size. After adding, the button turns into a check and the sheet folds straight back into the bar.

column4: Open-source star button with star history
column8: When an open-source project card scrolls into view, a line of the past year's star history draws in from the left, its end point breathing, and the star count rolls up digit by digit whenever someone else stars it. Press Star and the star icon spins as it fills yellow and the count goes up by one, while a ring spreads from the chart's end point and a “Today +1” bubble pops up. Press again to empty the star and bring the count back down.
As you scroll, each card comes to rest at the top, and while the next card slides over it, the one underneath shrinks, darkens and recedes. By the last card the stacked cards form steps.

Each sentence in an AI answer ends with a small numbered badge. Rest the pointer on a number and that sentence gets underlined while a source preview card floats above, highlighting the quoted part of the original, and the matching card in the source list below lifts up too. Rest the pointer on a source card and every sentence that used it is marked at once.

A cookie consent banner rises from the bottom of a website. Press Settings and the banner grows upward to show Essential, Analytics and Marketing switches, with Essential always on and locked. Press Accept all or Save choices and a bite mark appears in the cookie as crumbs fall, then the banner slides away, leaving a small cookie button in the bottom left to reopen the settings any time.

A faint grid lies behind a dark hero, and beams of light glide along its lines horizontally and vertically, leaving a tail before fading out. Move the cursor and only the grid around it softly lights up, while the headline and button in the middle sit crisply on top. With reduced motion, only the grid and headline are shown, without beams.

Every few seconds a new order slides in at the top of an order table and glows briefly as the rows below glide down. Press the Amount or Time header and the rows slide past each other into the new order while the sort arrow spins. Press Pause at the top and new orders just pile up; resume and “N new orders” come in all at once.

Move the cursor over four feature cards on a dark screen and a soft glow centered on it spreads along the card borders while lightly brightening their insides. The light crosses the gaps between cards to tint the edges of neighboring cards too, as if one lamp were shining on them all, and fades slowly once the cursor leaves.

In a landing page's terminal window, an install command types itself out one character at a time as if by hand; at Enter, download and setup lines spin in turn before turning into checks while a progress bar fills. Next a run command types in, the server starts and a local address lights up, and clicking that address pops a small browser preview out beside it. Replay starts it over.

column4: Order summary that recalculates with a promo code
column8: In a checkout order summary, press “Have a promo code?” and an input slides open below. Apply a code that doesn't work and the field shakes its head with a red note; apply a valid one and the field folds into a code pill, a discount line slips in, and the total counts down while the old amount gets struck through and a “You saved” pill pops out. Press the × on the pill to put everything back.

Below a landing page hero, the product screen starts small and tilted back, then stands up, grows and casts a deeper shadow as you scroll down until it faces you flat. Once it's flat the chart bars inside fill up, and scrolling back up lays it down again. The hint arrow at the bottom disappears once you start scrolling.

Press Sign in with a passkey on a login card and a device check sheet rises from below, its fingerprint pattern lighting up ring by ring from the outside as it reads. When the read finishes the fingerprint turns into a check, the sheet slides down, and the login card moves on to a welcome screen as your name floats in. Press Cancel on the sheet and it simply slides away, back to the start.

In the big input box on an AI product's first screen, example prompts type themselves out, erase and change, while a glowing border slowly circles it. Press a suggestion chip below to type that prompt into the box, then press send and the arrow turns into a spinner as a generating card unfolds below with shimmering lines.

In a landing page's customer logo grid, every few seconds one cell's logo blurs out upward while a new one sharpens in from below. The same logo never shows in two cells at once, and resting the pointer on a cell stops the swapping while a See story link slides out in that cell.

column4: AI TL;DR that folds long text
column8: Press Summarize above a long meeting note and a glowing line sweeps down the text, highlighting the key sentences one by one. Once it's read through, the body folds away and a three-line summary card unfolds in its place, its items writing out line by line as the reading time changes from 4 minutes to 20 seconds. Press Show original to unfold the text again, highlights included.

Scroll to the end of the page and the content rises like a curtain to reveal a dark footer fixed beneath it. As it's revealed the footer grows slightly and brightens, and the big brand wordmark at the bottom floats up. Enter an address in the footer's newsletter field and press Subscribe to turn the button into a check.

A campaign headline slides up line by line from under an invisible mask, and once the last line lands a hand-drawn underline is sketched in. Move to the next copy and the current lines slip out upward while the new ones rise in from below, one after another.

At the top of a service status page, “All systems operational” sits beside a green pulse, and below it API, Dashboard, Payments and Webhooks each show the last 30 days as a row of 30 small bars. The bars grow in from the left as the page opens, and resting the pointer on one shows that day's uptime and any incident in a bubble. Press a component to unfold its past incidents below.

In a developer docs API example, choose the cURL, JavaScript or Python tab and the same request switches to code in that language. Press Send request and a glowing dot flies from the code to the response pane, where 200 OK and the elapsed time appear before the JSON response writes itself out line by line with keys and values in different colors. The copy button copies the code for the current language.

Press Add to cart on a product page and the cart drawer slides in from the right, with the item you just added flashing. The bar at the top is filled toward free shipping, and raising a quantity rolls the subtotal while the bar fills completely and turns into a free-shipping message. Removing an item slides its row out and folds it away, and pressing outside or close tucks the drawer back in.

While you scroll vertically, the view stays pinned and the strip of panels inside flows sideways. The big numbers and shapes in each panel trail slightly behind the strip for a layered feel, and the progress bar and step dots below move along.

column4: Category chip bar that follows scroll
column8: Like a delivery app's menu, a row of category chips sticks to the top; scroll the menu below and the underline slides to the chip for the section you're in, while the chip row nudges itself sideways to keep that chip in view. Press a chip to glide down to that section's heading, and scroll back to the top to lose the chip bar's shadow and see the big store header again.

A row of security and compliance badges at the bottom of a product page gets a passing sheen now and then. Press a badge and the card flips to show the certifying body, scope and validity; press Verify and a ring spins before a green check stamps the time it was checked. Press again to flip back.

column4: Form validation that takes you to errors
column8: Press Sign up at the bottom of a sign-up form and a summary such as “4 fields need attention” drops in at the top, while the wrong fields shake with red outlines and their hints unfold. The form glides up to the first wrong field and puts the cursor there, and pressing an item in the summary jumps straight to that field. Fixed fields fold their hint and gain a check as the summary count drops, and once everything is fixed the sign-up completes.

Switch the line and every letter slot spins through random symbols before settling into place from left to right. Hover the headline to scramble and decode it once more, and pick from three decoding speeds.

Eight years of drink sales play out as a bar race: bars that grow slide upward, swapping places with the row above as they lengthen. Bars pushed out of the top six slip away below, while the big year in the lower right and the numbers at the bar tips tick forward together. Pause and drag the year bar below to rewind or skip to any year.

Under the headline, a small round-cornered intro video stays pinned while widening to both sides as you scroll down, keeping its rounded corners until it nearly spans the card. Once it's full size it switches to playing, with a progress bar running and a caption rising, and scrolling back up shrinks it into a small card again.

column4: Feature request board that reorders on votes
column8: A product site's feature request board. Press the arrow on the left of an item and the number rolls up by one with a floating +1, and once its votes beat the row above, the item glides up a place. Press again to take the vote back and it slides back down, and each item carries a colored status badge such as In progress or Under review.

Type a title and description in page settings and the search result preview below follows each keystroke, while the bar under each field fills toward the recommended length. Make the title too long and its bar overflows in red as the preview title is cut off with an ellipsis. Press the Link share tab above to switch to the card you'd see when pasting the link into a messenger.

Change anything in the store settings and a “2 unsaved changes” bar drops from the top, its count rolling as you go. Try to leave for another menu without saving and the bar shakes and flashes red, asking you to decide first. Press Save and the button spins before the bar turns green with Saved and slides up; press Discard and the changed fields flash as they return to their original values.

Scroll through a features section and the cards entering the screen rise from below at short intervals starting from the left column, while the icon in each card pops and grows slightly. The section title's underline draws in from the left as it arrives, and scrolling back up then down again replays the entrance from the start.

Every few seconds a streak of light sweeps across the announcement pill above the hero headline, and its message rolls up to the next piece of news. Hover it and the border brightens as the arrow nudges forward; press it and the pill unfolds downward as the three latest updates drop in one by one. Press again to fold it back into a pill.

In the bottom left of a store page, a notice like “Kim from Busan just bought a linen shirt” pops up with a product photo, and once the bar beneath it runs out it fades away and another purchase shows up a little later. Rest the pointer on it to stop the bar, and press close to fold it away, after which a brief “Stop showing these” confirmation appears.

In a document's share dialog, press the link access button to open a list; choose Anyone with the link and the lock icon spins into a globe as the description and color change with it. Press Copy link and the link field flashes while the button turns into a check, and the Email, Message and Embed buttons below pop in one after another. The people working on it and their permissions are listed too.

A task board with To do, In progress and Done columns. Pick up a card and it tilts slightly and lifts; drag it over another column and a gap opens where it will land as the cards below shift down. Drop it and the card settles into the gap while each column's count updates, and cards dropped in Done get a check and a line through their title.

Entering a portfolio site, a big percentage climbs to 100 with small hesitations while a thin bar fills beneath it. When it's full, the loading screen splits into top and bottom halves that slide away, revealing the site's first screen where the name, photo and headline rise one after another. Use Reload to watch it from the start.

In a site builder's preview, choose desktop, tablet or mobile, or drag the handle on the right, and the frame's width changes smoothly while the ruler above shows the current width. As it narrows, the page's three-column cards rearrange into two columns and then one, the menu folds into a hamburger button, and the ruler mark flashes each time you cross a breakpoint.

When the photo gallery opens, each tile first shows a tiny blurry preview while a thin bar below fills as data arrives. Once a photo has fully loaded, the blur lifts and it shrinks slightly into place, sharp, and its name floats up. Turn on slow connection and reload to watch the same process slowly, so you can feel how waiting works without empty boxes.

Read down a blog post and from the third paragraph the text fades and cuts off, with a membership card below letting you know you've used this month's free articles. Choose monthly or yearly to change the price, and press Start free: the button spins briefly, the card folds away, and the hidden paragraphs clear up and unfold down the page.

A large sentence sits in faint gray, and as far as you scroll, its words fill in with solid color one at a time from the start. Key words bloom with color the moment they fill, and once you have read to the end a next button floats up below. Scroll back up and they fade again.

In a product review summary, the average rating fills the stars down to the decimal, and bars for 5 down to 1 star grow to their share. Press a bar and only that row stays bold while the review list below switches to reviews with that rating; press it again to return to all reviews. Each review's Helpful button adds one when pressed.

column4: Store locator map synced with a list
column8: A store finder shows pins on a map up top and a list of stores below. Rest the pointer on a store in the list and its pin bounces and grows; press it and the map glides over to that pin as an info bubble opens with an open-now badge. The other way round, pressing a pin on the map scrolls the list to that store and makes it flash.

column4: Flowing gradient headline and thinking text
column8: A color gradient slowly flows through the highlighted word of a section headline, and in the AI reply bubble below, a bright sheen repeatedly sweeps across the gray ‘Thinking…’ text. Pick one of three color sets with the chips above — flowing light, rainbow or gold — and the headline and button text change together; when the answer is ready the shimmer stops and the real sentence appears.

Type @ in a sign-up form's email field and common email domains fan out as chips that fill in when pressed. End with a common typo such as gmial.com and a “Did you mean gmail.com?” suggestion drops down with the mistake marked; press it and the letters fix themselves as a check draws on the right of the field.

A product page's delivery note counts down “Order within 1 h 23 min for delivery tomorrow” by the second, while the bar below shrinks with the time left before today's dispatch cutoff. Change the address to Jeju and the headline flips to the day after tomorrow, a note replaces the countdown, and a ferry step slides into the delivery steps below so the truck goes that much farther.

In a five-stripe palette generator, press Shuffle and the unlocked stripes wash into new colors one after another, their color codes changing with them. Stripes you lock stay put, and pressing a stripe copies its code with a small notice. The preview below paints its buttons, card and background with the current palette right away to show how it would actually look.

Press the globe button in the site header and a language list drops down; choose Korean, English or Japanese and the menu, headline, description and button text slide up and out from top to bottom, swapped for the new language. Buttons whose labels change length widen and narrow smoothly, and the list shows a check next to the chosen language.

Type @ in a comment box and a list of teammates pops out right under the cursor, narrowing by name as you keep typing with the matching letters in bold. Choose with the up and down arrows and press Enter or click, and @name becomes a highlighted mention in your text while the people who'll be notified stack up as avatars below.

Press Delete in a project's danger zone and a warning dialog appears; the delete button only turns on once you type the project name exactly. The name above the field fills in red as you type it correctly, and a wrong letter shakes the field. Deleting scatters the project card behind into fragments as it vanishes, leaving a notice with an Undo button whose remaining time shrinks.

Small UI pieces float around the product screen in the middle: a payment alert, a teammate's cursor, a revenue chart and a rating. Move the cursor and each piece shifts away by a different amount depending on its depth, creating a sense of space, and left alone they each bob up and down slowly. Every few seconds the payment alert shows a new amount.

A product's changelog page. Versions and dates run down a vertical timeline, and the newest entry at the top has a blinking new dot. Choose the New, Improved or Fixed chip at the top and the highlight pill slides over to it, while entries that don't match fold away and the rest close up.

column4: Install command tabs by package manager
column8: In a docs page's install box, choose the npm, pnpm, yarn or bun tab and the pill underneath slides over while only the changing characters of the command fade and rewrite. Press Copy and the icon turns into a check as a Copied bubble floats up, and the next-step code unfolds line by line below. Your chosen tool is remembered next time.

column4: Detail side panel from a list row
column8: Press a row in a customer list and a detail panel slides out from the right while the row stays highlighted. Move to the previous or next customer with the arrows at the top of the panel or the J and K keys, and the content swaps up or down in the direction you went as the list highlight follows. Press outside or Esc and the panel tucks back in.

column4: Button that morphs into a form
column8: Press ‘Get the newsletter’ and the button stretches sideways into an email field with a send button. Send it and the whole thing shrinks into a circle whose ring spins before a check is drawn, then it opens back out into a ‘Subscribed’ pill. If the format is wrong, the field shakes its head.

Scroll the body and the chapter you are reading darkens in the table of contents on the right, while a vertical marker grows and shrinks to cover however much of that chapter is on screen. When two chapters are visible the marker spans both, and pressing an entry scrolls smoothly to that chapter.

In a list of project names set in large type, hover over a row and that project's photo floats up beside the cursor, following a beat behind and tilting toward your motion. Move to another row and the photo strip slides up or down to the next image, while the chosen row shifts right to reveal an arrow. Focusing a row with the keyboard also floats its photo at the row's end.

Press Start in the middle and the number flickers while ping is measured, then the needle sweeps up for the download, trembling as the arc fills with color. After the needle drops back to zero the upload climbs again in another color, while the tiles below sketch the live speed as a small line before settling on the average. The scale stretches section by section so 0–1000 Mbps reads evenly.

On a pricing page, drag the team size bar and a number bubble follows along while the total below rolls digit by digit. Cross the 10 and 30 marks and the plan name moves from Starter to Team to Business as the per-seat price drops, and the newly unlocked feature line sparkles. Switch to yearly billing and the amount becomes a full year, with a savings badge popping out.

column4: Booking slot that splits to confirm
column8: In a call booking widget, pick a day from the date strip and that day's open times rise from below one after another. Press a time and its button shrinks to half as a Confirm button slides out beside it; press Confirm to move to a booked screen summarizing the date and time. Fully booked days are dimmed and blocked.

Write a prompt and press Generate: four tiles fill with coarse noise, and as the step count climbs the noise clears and blurry blobs of color resolve into crisp pictures. Each tile's progress rises on its own so they finish at slightly different times. Pick the one you like and it gains an outline while Vary turns on; press it and the other tiles regenerate as new pictures in the same palette.

A highlighter sweeps across the key phrases of a paragraph from left to right, one after another. A phrase that wraps is filled to the end of the first line before continuing on the next, and longer phrases take longer. Change the pen and the strokes bleed into the new color; ‘Redraw’ lifts them off and paints again from the start.

As a photo scrolls into view, a narrow slit in the middle widens to both sides to reveal it, while the image inside scales down slightly so it seems to approach. The caption rises from below just as the slit finishes opening, and scrolling back up closes it again.

On a subscription settings screen, pressing Cancel subscription raises a dialog asking why you're leaving, and choosing a reason turns on Next. Next slides in an offer card matched to your reason: a discount if price is the issue, or a pause if you rarely use it. Accept it and a check draws itself before the dialog closes and the plan card behind it updates with the discounted price and a badge.

A connect-your-domain screen lists the DNS records you need to add, each value with a copy button that turns into a check when pressed. Press Verify and DNS lookup, global propagation and certificate issuance each spin in turn before turning into checks, with the region dots on a small map lighting up green one by one during propagation. When everything is done, a lock and https appear in the address and the domain is connected.

In a workspace's member settings, enter an email, choose a role and press Invite: a new row pushes in at the top of the member list with a blinking Pending badge. A moment later the person accepts, color fills their gray avatar, the badge turns to Joined and the member count goes up by one. Pressing an existing member's role button switches between Editor and Viewer.

Press the hamburger on a mobile site and its three lines turn into an X as the menu drops down with items rising one by one. Press an item that has a submenu and the next list slides in from the right while the current one shifts slightly left, with the back button and location title at the top changing too. Press back to return the opposite way.

Press Run audit and a filmstrip below captures the page drawing itself in time order, from blank to skeleton to finished, frame by frame, with a marker dropped at the moment the largest image appears. When the audit finishes, the Performance, Accessibility, Best practices and SEO rings above draw to their scores as the numbers climb, colored green, orange or red by score. The metric bars below fill alongside their thresholds too.

On a store's product page, the long product details are only partly shown and fade out at the bottom. Press Show more and the details area smoothly grows to its real length as the fade lifts, while the button moves down and turns into Show less. When you collapse it, the height shrinks while the screen returns to the start of the details, so you never lose your place.

Press the person-shaped button in the corner of a website and a display settings panel unfolds. Raise the text size and the page text behind grows smoothly; turn on high contrast and the background and text get bolder; turn on link highlighting and every link gains an underline and outline. You can widen line spacing too, and Reset brings every setting back together.

Instead of firing the browser's notification prompt right away, a card with a wiggling bell first asks, “Want a heads-up when someone replies?” Press Turn on and the browser's permission box drops in at the top with an arrow pointing at Allow; allow it and the bell turns into a check as a first notification slides in from the top right. Press Later and the card folds into a small bell button.

column4: Link shortener that folds long URLs
column8: Paste a long address and press Shorten: its characters get pulled toward the middle and fold away, and a short link pops out in their place. Press Copy and the link field flashes as the button turns into a check. The new link slots in at the top of the recent links list below, where each row grows a small bar chart of its clicks over the last 7 days.

Pick a filter and the tiles that don’t match shrink away while the rest slide forward in order to fill the gaps. Tiles that come back pop up in their own spot, and the count beside the chips rolls to the number left.

Press the compare check on products in a list and a compare tray rises from below as the chosen items pop into its empty slots. With two or more in it, Compare turns on; press it and a comparison table unfolds from below, with a Best badge on the top value for weight, battery and price. Try to add more than three and the tray shakes to show the limit.

At first the phone’s glass, display, logic board, battery and back float apart in layers at an angle, each linked to a label by a line. Scroll down and the layers come down one at a time and lock together while the labels fold away, and once it is assembled the screen switches on.

column4: Contact form that adapts to the request
column8: Choose Sales, Support or Partnership at the top of a contact form and the pill slides over while the fields below fold and unfold into questions for that type. In Support, pressing Attach screenshot adds a file chip whose upload bar fills. The ring beside the message box fills with the characters you've typed, and Send moves you to a received card with a ticket number.

Scrub up and down the letter index at the right of a contact list and a large letter bubble follows to the left of your fingertip as the list jumps straight to that letter group. Index letters near the fingertip bow out to the left and grow so you can see exactly where you are, and when you let go the bubble fades while the group header stays pinned at the top.

In a page builder, press Hero, Features, Pricing, Testimonials or Footer in the block list on the left and that block's wireframe unfolds onto the canvas on the right. Rest the pointer on a block for up, down and delete buttons; moving a block slides it past its neighbors, and deleting folds it away. The block count and a Saved indicator blink at the top.

Press the Get stub on the right of a ticket-shaped coupon and it tilts and tears away along the dotted line, revealing the coupon code and a copy button in its place. Press copy and the button turns into a check while a saved-to-wallet notice rises from below. Above, the time left until the coupon expires counts down by the second.

column4: Usage meter that warns near the limit
column8: On a plan usage screen, the API call count climbs live as its bar fills, and past 80% the bar turns orange while a “You're close to your limit” strip drops down. Turn on the forecast and dashed segments extend from each bar to the projected end-of-month use, with the date it'll run over attached to anything that will. Rest the pointer on a bar for exact numbers.

Type the name you want and .com, .io, .app, .co and .dev rows rise from below one by one, each spinning a small ring before showing a price and an Add button if it's free, or dimming with an In use tag if someone has it. Press Add and the button turns into a check while the cart count in the top right bounces up.

A tool for optimizing photos before they go on your site. Switch the format to WebP or AVIF or move the quality bar, and the original and result size bars shrink right away while the savings percentage rolls. Drag the divider in the middle to compare the original and optimized photo side by side; push quality too low and the result side turns mushy with a warning.

Turn on comment mode in a site preview and the pointer becomes a crosshair; click anywhere and a numbered pin drops with a bounce as a comment box opens beside it. Post the comment and the box folds into the pin while the comment count in the top right goes up. Click a pin again to open its bubble, and Resolve turns the pin into a green check and fades it.

In a site's font settings, pick the Modern, Editorial, Tech or Classic pairing and the preview's heading and body fonts blur slightly and sharpen into the new pair. Change the size ratio and the heading, subheading and body sizes grow or shrink smoothly to that ratio, with each step's size marked on the scale at the right. Copy CSS copies the current setup as variables.

Type a street or building name into a shipping form's address field and a result list unfolds below, with the part matching your typing in bold. Choose a result and the postal code and address slide into place, while a detail field opens underneath and the cursor moves to it. Fill in the details and the save button turns on.

column4: Filter drawer with live result count
column8: On a mobile product list, press Filter and a drawer rises from below to set price range, color and size. Whatever you change, the “Show N items” count on the button rolls immediately, and the button is blocked when nothing matches. Press it and the drawer slides away as the list keeps only the matching items and re-settles, with your choices pinned at the top as removable chips.

In the middle of an integrations section sits the product logo, while tool icons such as mail, calendar and payments slowly circle it on an inner and an outer orbit, turning in opposite directions. The icons stay upright as they go, and resting the pointer on one stops the orbits, draws a line of flowing data between it and the center logo, and changes the caption above to that tool.

Only the key word at the end of the sentence is deleted and retyped like a typewriter. Korean is typed jamo by jamo the way an IME composes it, and the underline color changes with each word. The caret blinks while idle and holds still while typing.

Switch views and the photo tiles never vanish: each glides to its new spot and size as the layout moves between grid and list. The photos grow or shrink to fit their new slots, and the descriptions shown only in the list fade in beside them once the photos have settled.

Scroll inside and the sky, far mountains, near mountains and forest move at different speeds to create depth, while the sun sets with the scroll and the sky warms into dusk. The title sinks behind the mountains, then body cards rise over the forest and cover the scene.

A headline where a moving scene shows through only the big title letters. Pick ocean, sunset or forest with the chips below and the scene inside the letters changes smoothly, and the play button pauses or resumes the motion. Hover the headline and the scene inside the letters drifts slightly toward the cursor.

Enter a store and an event popup bounces up in the middle, its three banners sliding sideways every few seconds as the dots and page count below follow along. You can drag the banners across too, and pressing Don't show today shrinks the popup down into a gift button in the bottom right with a “See you tomorrow” note.

Hover a big menu word and it splits horizontally: the top half slides up, the bottom half slides down, and a line of description unfolds in the gap. The closer the cursor is to the middle of the word, the wider it opens, and moving keyboard focus opens it the same way.

column4: Coffee cup that fits its size
