column8: Pick a size and the cup stretches or shrinks into its new shape while coffee pours in as a stream and settles at the right level. Each extra shot darkens the coffee, and switching on milk tops it with a white foam layer. The price rolls to its new value.

A small round cursor follows across the screen like a spring, stretching to wrap a button's shape over buttons and thinning into a vertical bar over text. Over a photo it swells into a large circle that says View, and over a link it becomes a dot holding an arrow. While wrapping a button it is pulled slightly toward your fingertip so it feels stuck to your hand.

Pick up a file and drag it toward the bin: the closer it gets, the more the lid twitches open, and dropping it there sends the file spinning small into the bin as the bin gives a shake. The count stacks up on a badge, and ‘Undo’ pops the last file back out of the bin to its place.

Pull the block on the end of the wall-mounted spring and let go: it bounces with the stiffness and damping you set while the graph below draws its position live. More stiffness vibrates faster; less damping wobbles longer. Tap a preset and the sliders glide to its values while the block immediately demonstrates.

Change the sort and the rows don’t jump all at once; each glides to its new place. Rows moving up lift slightly toward you while rows moving down recede, so overlapping paths never get confusing. The number in the sorted column is highlighted by how far each row moved.

Scroll down and a winding route is drawn just that far, with a little plane following the tip of the line, facing its heading. Reach a stop and its dot grows as a card with the city and date unfolds; scroll back up and the route is taken back in.

A gradient background where five pools of light overlap and blend as they drift slowly across a dark sky. Hover and one light trails after your cursor while the others lean toward it, and switching palettes melts the colors over gradually instead of swapping at once. A fine film grain sits on top.

Rub the silver coating of a lottery ticket with the cursor and it peels away wherever you scratch, gradually revealing the prize beneath while silver flakes fly from the spot. Scratch more than half and the rest lifts away at once as the result pops out, with confetti bursting for a win. Press New ticket to cover it again with a different result.

Press another page in the site's top menu and a colored curtain rises from the bottom to cover the screen, the destination page's name briefly appears on it, then the curtain lifts away to reveal the new page. The new page's title and image rise one after another as the curtain clears, and the menu's current-location marker slides over too.

Below a store's search box, a single line rolls through the live trending searches from #1 every few seconds, each with an up, down or new marker beside its rank. Press the line and a top-10 list unfolds below; a moment later the ranking refreshes and the changed items slide past each other into their new places. Press a term and it's typed into the search box as the list folds away.

Move the cursor and a photo drops at every spot it passes, piling up at slight tilts before shrinking away a moment later. The faster you move, the denser the photos fall, while the large headline in the middle shows through between them. Press and a handful of photos fan out at that spot at once.

Tap an item in the list and the detail screen slides in from the right while the screen beneath recedes slightly to the left and dims. The large title shrinks and moves into the ‘Back’ label, and dragging from the left edge pulls it partway back under your finger, either returning or staying depending on where you let go.

Hover over an ordinary pricing card and a round x-ray lens follows the cursor; inside it alone, the HTML and CSS that build the card show through in the same place. Over the title you see its heading tag, over the button its button code; press and the lens spreads across the whole card into a code view, and press again to come back.

A 100-cell waffle chart shows how 100 people commute; switch the age group above and only the cells that change hands flip one by one along a diagonal wave into their new color. The percentages in the legend on the right roll to their new values, and hovering or pressing a legend item leaves only that mode's cells in focus.

Tap the title and the letters are sliced into horizontal bands that slip out of line, while red and cyan channels split apart and snap back together. Turn on ‘Unstable’ and it jitters at irregular intervals; the strength slider sets how far the slices drift.

Tap a destination card and it grows from where it sits to fill the screen: the photo stretches into the header and the title moves to the big-title spot. The body rises in line by line, and closing retraces the same path to shrink back into the card.

Scroll through the product and at every section the whole background blends into the next flavor’s color, while the drink can pinned in the middle turns to match and its label and name change. The color never jumps between sections; it keeps blending as far as you scroll.

A space scene where stars fly out toward you from the center. Hold down and the speed builds until the stars stretch into long streaks that shift blue, as if jumping to warp, then ease back to cruising speed when you let go. Move the cursor and the heading bends slightly that way.

Flick the eight-slice prize wheel with your hand or press Spin and it whirls fast before friction gradually slows it down. The pointer at the top clicks back each time a slice boundary passes, and when it stops the winning slice glows as the result rises. The harder you flick, the longer it spins.

Scroll the list up and the large title slides up and turns into a small title in the middle of the top bar, while the search field compresses and disappears. From that moment the bar gains frosted glass and a hairline. Pull further at the top and the large title stretches a little like a rubber band.

Hold the mic button to start recording: the timer runs and a waveform sized to your voice slides in from the right. Keep holding and slide left, and ‘Slide to cancel’ fades until, past the line, a trash can rises from below and opens its lid, a red recording blob arcs over and drops in, and the lid shuts as the can gives a little shake. Simply let go and a voice message bubble pops up in the chat.

Drag up the lid of a laptop lying closed on a desk and it swings open in 3D around its hinge. Past a certain angle the screen shows a logo and progress bar, then the desktop and a window light up in turn while the keyboard backlight glows softly. Lower it again and the screen dims to sleep; a press opens or closes it all the way.

When the cursor enters any of nine project tiles, a caption panel slides in from the edge the cursor crossed and covers the tile. Enter from the top and it drops from the top, from the left and it sweeps from the left, and on leaving it pulls away toward the side the cursor exited. The panel seems to travel from tile to tile with the cursor.

Drag the bottom sheet over the map and it tracks your finger, then carries the release velocity into the nearest of three heights — collapsed, half or full — overshooting slightly like a spring before settling. Drag past the ends and it resists like a rubber band; open it fully and the map behind shrinks a little and dims.

On a map of seventeen regions laid out as hex tiles, the blossom front climbs north from Jeju to Gangwon as the days roll by, each tile turning from bud green through deep-pink full bloom to pale pink and then leafy green. Petals drift off tiles in bloom, and the date and count of blooming regions in the upper right change along with it. Drag the date bar below to any day, and hover a tile to see that region's bloom date and stage.

The key word sits on one face of a 3D box, and each change rolls the box downward to show the next face. As it rolls, the top face darkens and the front brightens, and the caption below turns over too. A progress bar fills while it advances on its own, and hovering pauses it.

Popular template cards run sideways, with the next card peeking in on the right. Drag the row and it follows your hand; let go and it glides as far as you flung it before snapping onto the nearest card. The arrows in the top right also move one card at a time, the progress bar below fills to show where you are, and the arrows dim at the start and end.

Scroll down and the keyhole in the door grows until you are inside the night scene beyond it, while the door is pushed out and blurs. Reach the end and the title rises in the scene as the stars twinkle; scroll back up to slip out through the keyhole.

Drifting dots link up with faint lines whenever they come close, weaving a constellation-like mesh. The cursor becomes a node too, joining nearby dots with brighter lines and gently drawing them in; press and a burst of new dots scatters from that spot and blends into the mesh. The number of lines currently linked shows at top left.

Press the ribboned gift box and the bow slowly unties as the ribbons slide off both sides, then the lid pops up and tips over backward. Rays of light spread from inside as a gift coupon floats up amid flying sparkles. Press Wrap again and it packs itself back up in reverse.

Scroll far enough down and a round button floats up at the bottom right, its ring filling with how much you have read. Press it and the arrow inside becomes a rocket that blasts off with a flame, while the article glides smoothly back to the top.

Tap an empty spot on the map and a pin falls from above, sticks into the ground and bounces once, its shadow shrinking and growing with the height of the fall. A ripple ring spreads where it lands, and a card slides up with the address of that spot. Tap the pin to pluck it out.

A label wrapped around a round can bends along the cylinder as it turns, narrowing and darkening toward the edges for a sense of volume. Drag sideways and it spins with your hand, coasting to a stop when you let go. Change the flavor with the chips below to swap the label colors and fruit, and press Open to lift the tab as fizzy bubbles rise.

Hover over a large sentence and a round window follows the cursor; inside it alone, a different sentence in inverted colors shows through in the same place. Move fast and the window stretches slightly as it follows; press and it floods the whole frame to reveal the hidden sentence, then press again to shrink it back.

Press the video’s minimize button and the player shrinks into a small window that flies to the bottom-right corner while the list below slides up into the space. Drag and throw the small window and it projects its landing spot from your release speed, springing onto the nearest of the four corners; push it hard toward the side and it tucks half off-screen, leaving just a handle to pull it back.

Text set along a circular path turns slowly; hover and it speeds up, leave and it coasts back down with inertia. Press it and the center arrow springs up as the text changes, the new letters filling in one by one around the circle. The number below shows the current speed.

Move to the next photo and the frame breaks into a small grid, each cell popping in a piece of the new photo at its own moment until it is covered. Choose how the cells spread: a wave from the left, a ring from the center, or at random.

Press the padlock and the keyhole turns sideways like a key, then the shackle pops up and opens with one leg free. Press again and the shackle drops back with a click as the body squashes slightly and the keyhole turns back. Once shared, the people who can see it appear one by one next to you, and the description and color change with it.

The faster you scroll the list, the more its cards lean in that direction and stretch slightly, then spring upright the moment you stop. Scrolling slowly barely tilts them so reading is undisturbed, and the gauge at the top shows the current speed.

A generative drawing where countless particles drift along an invisible current, leaving silky trails. The current slowly reshapes over time; hover and a vortex forms around the cursor, wrapping the particles around it. Press to switch the color scheme and start drawing anew.

Stamp a ten-slot coffee card and a rubber stamp comes down from above, presses firmly and lifts, leaving a round stamp at a slight angle with a touch of ink bleed. The progress bar below fills as slots do, and the tenth stamp flips the card over to reveal a free drink reward.

Hover a top menu item and a dropdown panel opens below; move to another item and instead of closing and reopening, the panel slides under it while changing size and position. The content inside slides sideways in the direction you moved, and the small caret on top follows the panel.

Start typing and three dots bob inside a cloud to show ‘Saving’; pause and they turn into a check that reads ‘Saved just now’. As time passes it switches to relative times like ‘Saved 10s ago’, and going offline draws a slash through the cloud with ‘Saved on this device’. Reconnect and a spinning arrow syncs it back.

Hover over a wristwatch photo and a round loupe follows the cursor, magnifying that spot so the dial's tiny lettering, tick marks and even the tip of the second hand come into sharp view. Each press switches between 2.5× and 4×, with the current power shown on the loupe's rim. The hands move with the real time.

Each letter of the headline changes weight and size with its distance from the cursor, so a bulge of bolder type rolls across the words around the cursor. Letter cells keep a fixed width so lines never wobble as letters thicken, and a press flips to the opposite mode where only the letters near the cursor thin out. When the cursor leaves, every letter eases back to regular weight.

Long-press a row in the conversation list and it sinks in slightly, then the screen behind blurs as a conversation preview card pops out of that spot and grows, with a quick-action menu unfolding below one item at a time. Keep holding, slide onto an action and let go to run it, or press the preview to expand it to full screen. Pinning slides that row up to the top.

Eight departments' satisfaction last year and this year are joined by slope lines between two posts, drawn one after another from left to right when the chart first appears. Risers turn green and fallers red, and choosing Rank above slides each end from its score position to its rank position so the lines cross over each other. Hover a line or name to keep only that department and see how much it moved below.

Tap the word and its letters fly off in every direction, spinning and bouncing off the walls, hang there for a moment, then spring back into place. You can also grab a single letter and throw it; let go and it flies at that speed before coming home.

Move to the next slide and the frame splits into eight vertical strips that flip over one after another to reveal the new scene on their backs. The strip edges darken as they turn so you can feel their thickness, and depending on direction the left or right strips go first.

Three drums for AM/PM, hours and minutes roll like cylinders, and whatever sits on the middle line is selected. Let go and it settles neatly on the nearest slot, while the values above and below tilt and fade as if curving around the back of the drum. The alarm label and time remaining at the top update as you pick.

column4: Dot grid waves from the cursor
column8: Move the cursor over a tidy grid of dots and small ripples spread in rings from each spot you pass, the dots swelling, settling and blooming in color. Press to fire a big wave across the whole grid, and where several ripples meet they stack into larger swells.

On a snowy winter calendar, press any of the twelve little doors up to today and it swings wide on its hinge, revealing a hidden treat and a one-line message. Opened doors stay open, while doors for days yet to come shake with a padlock and stay shut. The count of doors left drops with each one you open.

column4: Waitlist position that moves up with referrals
column8: Enter a valid email in the beta waitlist card and the Join button turns on; press it and it spins briefly before the card flips to your waitlist position, the number racing up and settling. A row of dots below shows the people ahead and your spot, and each friend you invite rolls your position down by 100 as your dot slides forward and −100 floats up.

Move the cursor left and right over a thumbnail in a video list and the scene inside steps back and forth with your position, letting you skim a sunrise, a bike ride and a blooming flower. A progress bar fills beneath the thumbnail and the scene's timestamp floats above the cursor; when the cursor leaves, it returns to the cover frame.

Five-year age bars stack into a population pyramid, men on the left and women on the right, rolling from 1970 to 2070 as the broad-based triangle turns into a jar and then a top-heavy inverted triangle. The 1958 birth cohort is marked in yellow and climbs one row every five years, while the share aged 65+ and the median age above change along with it. Drag the year bar below to any year and hover a bar to see that age group's numbers.

Only the sentence under the cursor stays sharp while the others fade. As the focus moves, the bar on the left slides along, stretching and shrinking to the sentence’s height, and the counter above rolls to show which sentence you are on. ↑/↓ on the keyboard move one sentence at a time too.

Hover the stack of polaroids and it fans out slightly; tap it and the photos fly out into a neat grid. Tap one photo in the grid and the photos gather back into a stack with that one on top, each landing at a slightly different angle.

Scroll down and the vertical line in the middle fills with light from the top, and each year’s dot pops up and lights as the tip of the line reaches it. That year’s card slides in from alternating sides, and scrolling back up switches the line and cards off in reverse.

A map that draws slowly breathing terrain as contour lines. Hover and a hill rises under the cursor as the lines wrap around it in rings; press to raise a peak there, labeled with its height. Every fifth line is drawn bolder, and higher lines turn warmer.

Press an activity button and a +XP number pops out of it, flies into the experience bar and lands as the bar shimmers and fills. When the bar is full it flashes, the level number rolls upward, rings of light spread around it and a Level up banner appears before filling again from the leftover XP.

Five menu links each show a different underline motion: a line that draws in from the left and exits to the right, one that spreads out from the center, a straight line that turns into a flowing wave, two strands that cross as they pass, and a single dot that springs out into a line. The same underlines appear on keyboard focus.

Eight apps float as bubbles sized by revenue on axes of users and retention, sliding along their own paths each time a quarter passes. Drag the chart background left or right to wind time back and forth as the big quarter label behind follows, and press a bubble to leave a dotted trail of where it has been, making booms and busts easy to spot.

Press play and the captions pop in one word at a time on the beat of the speech, with key words swelling large before settling in color. When a sentence ends, its caption line folds up and away as the next one begins, and the waveform below rises and falls like a voice.

The bars at the top fill over time and the scenes advance on their own; tap the right side of the screen for the next scene and the left for the previous. Press and hold to pause and the header fades, and when one person’s story ends it turns to the next person like a rotating cube.

column4: Phone screens that follow the text
column8: The phone on the left stays pinned, and as you scroll the descriptions on the right, its screen slides up from below to match the feature you are reading. At each change the phone tilts slightly and settles, and the step bar beside it shows which feature you are on.

Hundreds of specks of light lie scattered, then spring in to assemble into the shape of a word. Bring the cursor close and the specks are pushed aside, opening a hole that closes again as you move away; press and they all fly to the positions of the next word to spell it out.

Fill today's slot among the week's seven and a check hops into place as the flame in the middle flares up, then settles one size larger while throwing off more sparks. The day count rolls up by one, and filling all seven slots makes a full-week badge sparkle. The flame keeps burning in three layers—outer, inner and core—each swaying its tip to its own rhythm.

Slide it and the face changes continuously: at the far left it frowns with brows pinched down, in the middle the brows relax and the mouth goes flat, and toward the right the corners rise until it breaks into an open-mouthed grin with eyes folded into crescents and blushing cheeks. The background tints along with it and the label rolls to the new level; press ‘Send’ and the face nods while a thank-you message rises in place of the label.

On a neighborhood map with a river and parks, 140 cafés gather into numbered clusters; zoom in and the clusters split into smaller groups and single pins that spread out to their places, then get pulled back together when you zoom out. Drag to pan the map, press a cluster to zoom one level in around it, and press a single pin to see the café's name and rating.

A line of text flows endlessly along a rippling wave. Change the wave height or flow speed and the curve is redrawn at once, with each letter leaning or standing up to match the slope. Whatever you type in the field rides the wave.

Press ‘Next’ and the next page’s color rises from the bottom as a rolling wave that covers the screen, then the illustration and text float up once it has passed. The crest sways side to side as it rises, and the dots below stretch to mark the current page.

Reach the end of the list and a bouncing three-dot loader appears before new cards float up from below one at a time and join the list. Meanwhile, when new posts pile up above, a ‘3 new posts’ pill slides down; tap it to glide to the top where the new posts shimmer.

A globe whose continents are stippled from thousands of dots turns slowly as visit signals ripple out from its cities. Drag and it follows your hand; let go and it glides on momentum before settling back to its own pace. Dots on the far side are drawn smaller and fainter for a sense of round depth, and hovering a city dot shows its name and current visitors.

Of six achievement medals, locked ones sit as gray discs with a padlock and a progress bar showing how far along you are. Press Unlock and the next medal's bar fills to the end, the medal shakes, the padlock pops off, and it regains its color as a ray of light sweeps across and sparks scatter. Press an unlocked medal and it flips over to show the achievement and the date it was earned, then flips back with another press.

Forty-two laptops are drawn as curves across five axes — price, weight, battery, performance and screen — unfolding from left to right when they first appear. Drag up or down on an axis to make a filter band that keeps only that range, sinking non-matching lines to gray, and add bands on more axes to stack conditions. A short press on an axis clears its band, and hovering the legend below highlights just that type.

The words of a quote float out of focus, then come into focus one after another as they settle into place. Move on and the current words blur away as if scattering, while the speaker’s name slides up from below. A bar at the bottom shows when it will move on by itself.

Hover one of five narrow vertical photo strips and it opens wide while the others narrow. Folded strips show only a sideways name; the moment one opens, its name stands upright and a description and button float up from below.

Scroll the text and the big chapter number on the left rolls continuously like a strip of digits to point at the next chapter, while the ring gauge below fills with how much of the current chapter you have read. The chapter title beneath the number slides up as it changes.

A chord diagram shows the messages six teams sent each other as arcs around a circle joined by ribbons, with the arcs growing around the rim and the ribbons weaving in when it first appears. Switch between last month and this month above and the arc lengths and ribbon widths stretch and shrink continuously; hover a team's arc to keep only its ribbons with sent and received counts below, or hover a ribbon to see the traffic both ways.

Draw sketchy underlines, circles, boxes and strike-throughs onto the key words of a sentence. Each mark is drawn twice, slightly wobbly, so it feels like a pen, and the words are marked one after another. Pick another style and the old marks are erased in reverse before the new ones are drawn.

An app download section detects your device and leads with a big button for that operating system. Switch the platform tabs above and the button's icon, label and version/size line flip upward to the new platform. Press Download and the button turns into a check, three install steps light up in turn, and an arrow bounces in the top right corner pointing at your downloads.

Three rows of big text drift slowly in opposite directions, then speed up with your scroll and lean slightly toward the motion. Scroll up and the direction flips; stop and they ease back to a lazy drift.

Twelve months of daily temperatures are stacked like overlapping mountain ridges, rising one after another from January when the chart first appears. Each ridge is tinted from blue to red by that month's average, and switching between 2005 and 2025 above slides every ridge to the right as the colors warm. Hover a month to bring its ridge into focus with a mean line, and see the average and the change from 20 years earlier below.

Spoiler phrases are covered in shimmering grains of sand; tap one and the grains scatter outward from that spot as the text appears. Phrases that wrap are covered line by line, and ‘Hide again’ gathers the grains back to cover them.

Sixty-four tiles form one picture, then flip in turn as a ripple spreads from where you press, turning into a different picture on their backs. Each tile tips over in the direction the wave travels, and tiles under the cursor lift slightly forward, rippling after your fingertip.

A scatter of study hours against scores carries a regression line and a confidence band; drag any point and the line tilts after it like a spring as the band widens or narrows, while the equation and R² above update instantly. Press an empty spot to add a point, and turn on Residuals to show each point's distance to the line as a vertical stroke, revealing how far-off points pull the line.

Words that come up most in café reviews gather in a cloud sized by how often they're mentioned; switch between January, April and July above and words that stay grow or shrink to their new size as they slide into new spots, words that drop out shrink away and new words pop in. Hover a word to keep only its group with its mention count and change from the previous month shown, or pick a whole group from the legend below.

Four small charts — visitors, conversion, average stay and response time — stack on the same 30-day axis, their lines drawn left to right when they first appear. Move the cursor over any of them and a vertical line sweeps across all four at once, updating each day's dots and values together, while dotted flags mark a deploy and a sale so a response-time spike and a visitor bump can be compared side by side. Turn on Compare to lay the previous 30 days underneath as faint dotted lines with a change rate next to each value.
